stem: A pharmacist learns at 3:00 p.m. Monday that a patient received the wrong warfarin strength. By when must the pharmacist initially document the quality-related event under 247 CMR 15.03(2)?

choices.text: Only at the next monthly staff meeting.
Only after the prescriber confirms injury.
Within 24 hours after discovery or notification of the event.

explanation.core_reasoning: The initial QRE documentation clock begins with discovery or notification and is 24 hours. The duty is not postponed until injury is confirmed or a later committee review occurs.

choice_analysis.A: A monthly meeting would be far too late for the initial documentation requirement.
choice_analysis.B: Seven business days is associated with other reporting frameworks, not this QRE documentation clock.
choice_analysis.C: Thirty days is not the 247 CMR 15.03(2) deadline.
choice_analysis.D: The documentation duty does not depend on confirmation of patient injury.
choice_analysis.E: This states the correct trigger and 24-hour period.

related_facts: Warfarin strength errors can create clinically significant anticoagulation risk.
QRE documentation is distinct from any separate serious-event report that might be triggered by injury or death.
explanation.mpje_trap: Different pharmacy-reporting systems use different clocks; anchor the deadline to the named QRE duty.

reasoning_steps: Identify that the event is a quality-related event
Start the clock at discovery/notification and apply the 24-hour documentation period
